-122.53400,37.94390.name: Marin Fertility Center
-122.53400,37.94390.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Peter S. Uzelac, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-104.57995,50.44791.name: Planned Parenthood Regina
-104.57995,50.44791.desc: A clinic mapped in OpenStreetMap as offering fertility treatment. OpenStreetMap holds what somebody chose to map, so a country with few points here may be thinly mapped rather than thinly served. That is the reverse of the national registers alongside it, which are close to complete for one country and silent everywhere else. This layer is a cross-check and a source of leads, not a count.

-96.58472,39.19744.name: National Bio and Agro-Defense Facility (NBAF)
-96.58472,39.19744.state: Kansas State Univeristy, Manhattan, KS 66502, United States
-96.58472,39.19744.company: US Department of Homeland Security, US Department of Agriculture
-96.58472,39.19744.desc: A BSL4 animal laboratory, under construction. Run by US Department of Homeland Security, US Department of Agriculture. It is categorised as a public health laboratory, working on animal health. Containment space: 4084 SqM. Operational or announced: Expected 2024. There is no international register of laboratories at this containment level and no obligation to declare one, so this record comes from a research project rather than a regulator. What that project could not find out is absent here too.

-0.63498,51.27975.name: High Containment Large Animal Facility (HCLAF)
-0.63498,51.27975.state: Pirbright, Woking, Surrey GU24 0NF, United Kingdom, United Kingdom
-0.63498,51.27975.desc: A BSL4 laboratory, operational. Run by Pirbright Institute. It is categorised as a public health laboratory, working on animal health. Personnel work in sealed cabinets, handling material through glove ports. Containment space: 257 SqM. It stands in a built-up area, with more than fifty thousand people living within two and a half miles. There is no international register of laboratories at this containment level and no obligation to declare one, so this record comes from a research project rather than a regulator. What that project could not find out is absent here too.

8.24700,49.99300.name: BioNTech
8.24700,49.99300.desc: Known for the COVID vaccine, but the underlying business is a platform for making mRNA and cell therapies to order, now with manufacturing in Germany, Singapore and Rwanda. The Rwandan plant matters most: production capacity for genetic medicine has never existed in Africa before, and where a thing can be made determines who can get it far more reliably than where it was invented.

-0.13400,51.49900.name: Home Office — animals in science statistics
-0.13400,51.49900.desc: The UK government’s annual count of animal procedures, published by species, severity and purpose. It is the most detailed national record of laboratory animal use in the world, and it exists because the UK legislated for it in 1986. Comparable data does not exist in the United States, where mice, rats and birds are excluded from the governing Act altogether.

-0.76670,48.08330.name: Charles River / Janvier — European breeding sites
-0.76670,48.08330.desc: The European rodent breeding operations supplying laboratories across the continent, extended when Charles River acquired Janvier Labs. Two companies now supply most of the laboratory rodents used in Europe and North America, so the genetic background of the animals behind a very large share of published biology traces to a handful of colonies.

-71.05890,42.36010.name: Bayer / Ginkgo — Joyn Bio nitrogen fixation
-71.05890,42.36010.desc: A joint venture to engineer nitrogen-fixing microbes for cereals, since wound down. Nitrogen fixation in maize would displace a large share of world fertiliser use, and the attempt failing tells you how hard the biology is rather than how small the prize was.

-71.05890,42.36010.name: Inari — SEEDesign platform
-71.05890,42.36010.desc: Multiplex editing that alters dozens of genes at once in a single plant. The carve-outs adopted across forty countries were written around single small changes that could plausibly have arisen in nature, and no framework anywhere has drawn a line at a number of edits — so a plant with fifty deliberate changes can be exempt where a plant with one inserted gene is not.

-77.02200,38.89400.name: Farm liability and the StarLink settlement
-77.02200,38.89400.state: Washington DC — US EPA, 1200 Pennsylvania Ave NW
-77.02200,38.89400.desc: StarLink maize was approved for animal feed and not for people, then turned up in taco shells in 2000. The recall and the settlements that followed cost hundreds of millions and are still the reference case for who pays when an engineered organism ends up where it was not approved to be: the answer was the developer, after litigation, and only that once.

-77.02200,38.89400.name: EPA — pesticide misuse and drift reporting
-77.02200,38.89400.desc: Herbicide drift is the commonest real-world harm attached to engineered crops, because tolerance traits exist to be sprayed. Reports go first to the state lead agency, usually the department of agriculture, which inspects and can fine; the EPA holds the national incident record. Report while the damage is fresh: symptoms fade, and residue on foliage is detectable for a limited period.

2.29600,48.85700.name: Sanofi — recombinant vaccines and insulin
2.29600,48.85700.state: Paris — 46 avenue de la Grande Armée
2.29600,48.85700.desc: Makes recombinant influenza vaccine in insect cells and insulin in engineered bacteria. Insulin is the oldest engineered consumer product there is, approved in 1982, and it remains the example most often used to argue that this technology has a fifty-year safety record.

7.76900,48.59400.name: Council of Europe — Oviedo Convention, Article 13
7.76900,48.59400.desc: The only binding multilateral instrument that prohibits modifying the human genome in a way that can be inherited. Ratified by 29 European states, and conspicuously not by the United Kingdom, Germany or Russia. Everywhere else the germline is governed by national law, professional guidelines or nothing, so this single article carries more weight than any other text on the subject.

116.30700,40.05000.name: Qi Biodesign
116.30700,40.05000.desc: Develops its own editing tools rather than licensing Western ones, and works on edited crops for the Chinese market. Chinese groups building an editing toolchain outside the CRISPR patent estate is the practical answer to a licensing regime that would otherwise decide who may commercialise an edited crop.

8.62700,45.81000.name: Accredited GMO laboratories — European Network of GMO Laboratories
8.62700,45.81000.state: Ispra, Italy — EC Joint Research Centre
8.62700,45.81000.desc: The EU reference network for GMO detection, which publishes the validated methods national laboratories use and lists them by country. A result from an ENGL laboratory is the standard evidence in an EU enforcement action, so this is where to start in Europe rather than a general food laboratory.

117.20090,39.10420.name: Boyalife–Sooam joint venture, Tianjin
117.20090,39.10420.desc: A joint venture between a Chinese biotechnology firm, the Korean dog-cloning foundation and two Chinese research institutions, announced as the world's largest animal cloning facility: pet and police dogs, racehorses and beef cattle for the open market, starting at 100,000 cattle embryos a year and stated as growing towards a million. Whatever the plant has actually produced since, the announcement itself marks the transition this facet is about. Cloning stopped being a demonstration that a thing is possible and became a production line with a capacity figure attached, and the unit being produced is an animal.

10.02270,45.13330.name: Avantea
10.02270,45.13330.desc: The Italian laboratory where the rhino embryos are actually made. Eggs collected in Kenya are flown to Cremona, fertilised by intracytoplasmic sperm injection using frozen semen from dead males, and grown to blastocysts there. It is a commercial reproductive biotechnology laboratory whose ordinary business is cattle and horses, and the transfer of that capability to a wild species is the reason the programme exists at all. Note the geography this creates: the animals are in Kenya, the embryos are made in Italy, the stem cell work is in Japan and Germany, and the consortium is coordinated from Czechia. The last two individuals of a subspecies are the subject of a supply chain.
